extracted.intended_audience: users of the Singular computer algebra system (mathematicians / programmers working with polynomials, ideals, modules and Groebner bases)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference entries for Singular functions: syntax, types, purpose, assumptions, notes, restrictions, and examples for commands manipulating rings, polynomials, ideals, modules, resolutions, maps, and related operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorize
rubrics_metrics.description: Second argument selects multiplicity behavior: 0 returns factors and multiplicities (first factor is a constant); 1 returns non-constant factors (no multiplicities); 2 returns non-constant factors and multiplicities. May be called with one argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not implemented for coefficient fields real, finite fields of type (p^n,a) and ZZ/m. Examples show integer constant factor separated and multiplicities returned as an intvec. See absFactorize and poly sections for related functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: farey
rubrics_metrics.description: Lift the first argument modulo the second to a rational a/b; returns the best approximation under the Farey condition (|a|,|b| <= sqrt(N-1)/2 equivalent condition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current coefficient field must be the rationals. When called on a list, returns list of farey applied elementwise. Example: farey(2,32003) -> 2. See chinrem section for related Chinese remainder lifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: fetch
rubrics_metrics.description: Map objects between rings by position: identity for rings and qrings; maps i-th variable of source to i-th variable of basering; if basering has fewer variables those map to zero; intvec args describe permutation of variables; negative numbers and fourth arg describe mapping of parameters; zero maps variable/parameter to 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coefficient fields must be compatible (see map). Compared with imap, fetch uses variable positions not names. Useful to change variable names/order or map objects between ring and quotient ring. Examples demonstrate mapping polynomials, vectors, ideals across rings. See imap and map sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: fglm
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute a reduced Groebner basis in the current ring for a given ideal in another ring by applying the FGLM algorithm (convert degree-ordering reduced Groebner basis to lexicographical, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes the input ideal is zero-dimensional and given as a reduced Groebner basis in the given ring; monomial ordering must be global. Only permissible differences between given ring and current ring are monomial ordering and permutation of variables/parameters. Main application: conversion can be much faster than direct lex computation. Example provided. See fglmquot, option, qring, ring, std, stdfglm, vdim.

rubrics_metrics.name: fglmquot
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute a reduced Groebner basis of the ideal quotient I:p of a zero-dimensional ideal I and a polynomial p using FGLM techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes I zero-dimensional and given as a reduced Groebner basis; p must be reduced with respect to I. Example demonstrates computing quotient Groebner basis. See fglm, option, quotient, ring, std, vdim.

rubrics_metrics.name: files, input from (< "filename")
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and execute the content of the file filename; shorthand for execute(read(filename)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: < "example" reads and executes file. See execute and read sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: find
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the first position of substring in string or 0 if not found; optionally start at given position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax accepts optional start position. Examples show case-sensitive search and concatenated substring expressions. See string section.

rubrics_metrics.name: finduni
rubrics_metrics.description: Return an ideal contained in the given ideal such that the i-th generator is a univariate polynomial in the i-th ring variable, with minimal degree for this property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes the ideal is zero-dimensional and given as a reduced Groebner basis in the current ring. Example demonstrates output of univariate polynomials. See option(redSB), ring, std, vdim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Float
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a coefficient ring of floating point (inexact) real numbers for ring definitions; Float() or Float(int,int) forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in ring declarations to set floating coefficient field. Examples show output comments describing coefficients and number of vars. See cring and ring sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: fprintf
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatted output to a link using a format control string (like printf family); conversion specifications similar to print with additions (%n and %2 produce newline without consuming an argument).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an additional argument is a list, it should be enclosed once more into list() because passing a list flattens by one level. See print, printf, sprintf, and string sections. Examples show formatting of lists, modules, matrices and use of links (stdout).

rubrics_metrics.name: freemodule
rubrics_metrics.description: Create the free module of rank n generated by gen(1),...,gen(n); returns module (the free generators as rows/vectors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: freemodule(3) returns generators [1], [0,1], [0,0,1]. A matrix from freemodule(3) is the 3x3 unit matrix. See gen and module sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: fres
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute a (not necessarily minimal) free resolution of an input ideal/module using Schreyer's algorithm; second arg n > 0 limits steps to n, n=0 computes whole resolution; returns a resolution object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional third argument chooses output mode: "complete" (default) compute whole syzygy module in each step; "frame" to compute only the frame; "extended frame" to compute first two terms of each generator w.r.t. induced monomial ordering; "single module" to reduce memory by returning only frames except last module. Input must be a standard basis. Reference and example provided; see minres, res, sres, syz, Free resolution appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: frwalk
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute a Groebner basis in the current ring for an ideal in a different ring by applying the fractal walk algorithm (for conversion between orderings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main application: compute lex Groebner basis from degree-ordering reduced Groebner basis faster than direct computation. Only permissible difference between input ring and active base ring is monomial ordering. Example provided. See fglm, groebner, qring, ring, std.

rubrics_metrics.name: gcd
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the greatest common divisor (gcd) of two expressions (int, bigint, number, or poly); result type matches argument type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not implemented for coefficient fields real and finite fields of type (p^n,a). The gcd of two numbers is their integer gcd; for polynomials computes polynomial gcd. Examples include gcd of polynomials, bigints, numbers. See bigint, extgcd, int, number sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: gen
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the i-th free generator of a free module (gen(i) -> generator vector).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to reference free module generators e.g. in modules produced by freemodule. Examples show combining polynomials with gen(i). See freemodule, int, vector sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: getdump
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the content of the entire file/link and restore all variables from it; for ASCII links equivalent to execute(read(link)); for ssi links only use on data previously dump'ed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrictions: not supported for DBM links or links connecting to stdin. Example shows dump/getdump restoring variables and reloading libraries (with redefinition notices). See dump, link, read sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: groebner
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute a standard basis (Groebner basis) of an ideal or module by a heuristically chosen method or specified method strings; returns same type as first argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible methods: direct methods "std" or "slimgb" without conversion; conversion methods "hilb" or "fglm" where an easy ordering Groebner basis is computed then converted. Additional string "par2var" converts parameters to extra variables before computation. option(prot) reports chosen method. Hint: since no uniform best method exists, test various methods for hard examples (e.g., change characteristic or substitute parameters). Examples demonstrate many method combinations and output diagnostics (criteria triggered, vdim). See related library functions and std, stdfglm, stdhilb, slimgb sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: help
rubrics_metrics.description: Display online help information for a given topic using current help browser; if no topic given displays manual title page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shortcut ? may be used. Topic can be manual index entry or name of a loaded procedure with help section; wildcards allowed. If no unique match, a warning is printed and no help shown. If procedure's help differs from manual, the newer procedure help is printed. Browser can be set via --browser option or system("--browser",...). Use system("browsers") to list browsers. Examples and fallback tips provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: highcorner
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the smallest monomial not contained in the ideal/module generated by the initial terms of given generators; for a standard basis this equals the smallest monomial not in the ideal/module; returns 0 if ideal/module not zero-dimensional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works also in global orderings but not very useful there. Note gives detailed characterization: if xi>1 then xi does not divide m; and after deleting terms divisible by xi*m for xi<1, the reduced generators generate I. Example shows usage with std(i). See dim and std sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: hilb
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the (weighted) Hilbert series of the base ring modulo the ideal or R^k modulo the module defined by leading terms of generators; various arities return full display or intvecs for n-th series; optional weight vector computes weighted Hilbert series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If called with one argument displays first and second Hilbert series plus additional info; with two/three args returns intvec. Last entry of returned intvec is not part of actual Hilbert series but used in Hilbert-driven standard basis computation (minimum weight or 0). If input is homogeneous w.r.t. weights and a standard basis, result is Hilbert series of original ideal/module. Examples show output and usage with weights. See Hilbert function, ideal, intvec, module, std, stdhilb sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: homog
rubrics_metrics.description: Two uses: (1) Test homogeneity: returns 1 for homogeneous input, 0 otherwise (weighted homogeneity if current ring has weighted ordering); (2) Homogenize polynomials/vectors/ideals/modules by multiplying monomials with suitable power of given ring variable (or compute weighted homogenization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homogenizing variable must have weight 1. Examples show homog on polynomials/ideals and composition homog(homog(i,z)) -> 1. See ideal, module, poly, vector sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: hres
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute a free resolution of an ideal using the Hilbert-driven algorithm; returns a minimal free resolution of R/I; with int k stopping after k steps returns list of modules Mi = module(Ai).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input ideal must be homogeneous. Accessing single elements of a resolution may trigger partial computations. Example demonstrates using hres(I,0) and retrieving syzygy modules. See betti, fres, lres, minres, mres, res, sres, module sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: imap
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity map on common subrings: maps between rings and qrings with compatible ground fields by identity on variables and parameters of same name and 0 otherwise; can map parameters to variables (unlike map and fetch which behave differently).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for mapping from homogenized ring to original ring or between rings with/without parameters. Compared to fetch which uses variable positions, imap uses names. Mapping of rational functions not polynomials is undefined (result depends on version). Examples show mapping ideals across rings with different declarations. See fetch, homog, map, qring, ring sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: impart
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the imaginary part of a number in a complex ground field; returns 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: in ring (complex,i), impart(1+2*i) -> 2. See repart for real part.

rubrics_metrics.name: indepSet
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute a maximal set U of independent variables for an ideal (given by a standard basis): output intvec where v[i]=1 iff x(i) is independent; size of maximal independent set equals dim(I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: U independent iff I ∩ K[U] = (0); maximal if dim(I) = #U. With second int argument returns list of all maximal independent sets (or those not enlargeable). Examples show indepSet with option(isSB) and eliminate checks. See ideal and std sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: insert
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert an expression into a list at the beginning, or after given position if third arg provided; returns new list (input unchanged).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show insert(L,4) and insert(L,4,2). See delete and list sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: interpolation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the reduced Groebner basis of the intersection of ideals l[1]^v[1],...,l[N]^v[N] using linear algebra methods; each ideal should be a maximal ideal of a point in the form variable_i - coordinate_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ring should be polynomial ring over Zp or Q with global ordering. Example computes ideal of a singular cubic through given points with multiplicities and verifies vanishing/substituted derivatives. See diff, fglm, intersect, std, subst sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: interred
rubrics_metrics.description: Interreduce a set of polynomials/vectors: input f1,...,fn; output g1,...,gs with s ≤ n, preserving generated ideal/module and with distinct leading terms; additional properties for global/local orderings and option(redSB) control divisibility/ecart behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outputs satisfy (f1,...,fn) = (g1,...,gs) and L(gi) != L(gj) for i!=j. In global ordering and option(redSB), L(gi) does not divide monomials of other gj; in local ordering with option(redSB), divisibility implies ecart ordering. Example begins on page. See option(redSB), ecart, leading term definitions.
